comment: Records Route 53 holds that Cloudflare does not, on purpose. `add` records are created by this stack; `allow` patterns are records other stacks write into the zone. zone_diff.py reads both. Values here are not secret.

add.reason: only Amazon (ACM) may issue certificates for the domain once Route 53 is authoritative; no wildcard certificates

null MX (RFC 7505): the domain receives no mail today (support@, hello@ and accounts@ already bounce, asks.yaml cloudflare-mail-and-ruleset); aws-ses-email replaces this with SES receiving through extra_records
no server sends mail as the domain yet; SES signs with DKIM (aligned for DMARC) and uses its own MAIL FROM subdomain, so this can stay

add.name: _dmarc
add.reason: the DMARC record asks.yaml (cloudflare-mail-and-ruleset) asked for: nobody can send mail as the domain

allow.reason: site stack: CloudFront alias for the apex

allow.name: www
allow.reason: site stack: CloudFront alias, 301 to the apex (www is NXDOMAIN on Cloudflare)
site stack: ACM certificate validation records (also copied into Cloudflare before the nameserver change)

allow.name: _*.www
allow.reason: site stack: ACM validation for www

allow.name: _*.grants
allow.reason: site stack: ACM validation for grants
